title: The game loop
objective: Keep the game's state in one object, calculate rectangle collisions, and manage the score and game over
story: You're at the last stop on Pixel Planet. You've learned to draw and to move things; now you'll put it all together and build a real **game loop**: move, catch collisions, collect points, and end the game when needed.

sections.title: The game's state in one place
The three steps of the loop
Rectangle collision (AABB)
sections.body:
Two rectangles collide if they overlap horizontally **and** vertically. We write that with four conditions:

```js
function hits(a, b) {
  return a.x < b.x + b.w &&  // a starts before b's right edge
         a.x + a.w > b.x &&  // a's right edge passes b's left
         a.y < b.y + b.h &&  // the same vertically
         a.y + a.h > b.y;
}
```

If even one of the four conditions is false, there's a gap between them. Exactly touching edges (`a.x + a.w === b.x`) don't count as a collision.

In games this is called the **AABB** (axis-aligned bounding box) test: it's very fast and good enough for most games. Even for round objects, the box around them is often used.

tasks.title: Do they collide?
tasks.prompt:
Write the `hits(a, b)` function: it returns `true` if two rectangles of the form `{ x, y, w, h }` overlap, and `false` if they don't.

Exactly touching edges don't count as a collision. The code below writes the result into `#info`.
hints: Horizontally: a.x < b.x + b.w && a.x + a.w > b.x
The same vertically with y and h. Join all four with &&.

tasks.title: When a meteor hits
tasks.prompt:
Meteors that touch the player cost lives. Write the `collide()` function:

- remove the meteors that touch the player from `game.meteors` (`filter`) and lower `game.lives` by 1 for each one removed.
- If `game.lives` is `0` or less, set `game.over = true` and write `Game over!` into `#info`.

The `hits` function is ready.
hints: const before = game.meteors.length; keep the old count first.

tasks.title: Restart
tasks.prompt:
Write the `newGame()` function: every time it's called it returns a **brand-new** state object:

```js
{ score: 0, over: false, stars: [ /* 3 stars */ ] }
```

The stars are at `(40, 30)`, `(100, 70)` and `(160, 40)`; each has `w` and `h` of `10`.

When the `#restart` button is clicked, `game = newGame()` and `#info` says `Score: 0`.
hints: Write the object inside the function and return it: a new object is created on every call.
On click: game = newGame(); then update #info.

challenge.title: Falling stars
challenge.prompt:
Stars are falling from above. Write the `update()` function:

- If the game is over (`game.over`), do nothing.
- Add each star's own `vy` to its `y`.
- Remove the stars that fall out of the bottom of the canvas (`y > canvas.height`) from the array; add 1 to `game.missed` for each one.
- When `game.missed` is `3` or more, set `game.over = true` and write `Game over! Missed: 3` into `#info`.
hints: At the very start: if (game.over) return;
The ones left: game.stars.filter((s) => s.y <= canvas.height)
Number missed: the old length - the new length

project_task.title: Collecting stars
project_task.prompt:
The ship should collect the stars it touches! The stars are now boxes: `{ x, y, w, h }`. `update()` and `draw()` are ready.

- `hits(a, b)`: do two rectangles collide (AABB)?
- `collect()`: removes the stars that touch the ship from `stars`, adds 1 to `score` for each and writes something like `Score: 2` into `#info`. When no stars are left, `#info` says `Well done! All the stars are collected.`
- `step()`: calls `update()`, `collect()` and `draw()` in order. The loop calls `step()` every frame.
hints: hits: a.x < b.x + b.w && a.x + a.w > b.x && a.y < b.y + b.h && a.y + a.h > b.y
collect: stars = stars.filter((s) => !hits(ship, s)); and add how many fewer there are to score.
